# Glossary

Purpose: plain-language definitions of the terms used in Longstead and its guides.

**Accumulation phase.** The years before retirement when you add money to your accounts. In Simulate, contributions and employer match are added each year through your retirement age.

**Active plan.** The plan the app is currently using. Accounts, Simulate, Withdraw and Council all read the active plan. Also called the active project.

**Analysis.** A saved copy of one question and answer from a Council chat, kept for the plan. Listed under a plan's View analyses.

**Bracket (tax bracket).** A range of income taxed at one rate. You pay each bracket's rate only on the part of your income inside that bracket.

**Bracket fill.** Adding income, such as a Roth conversion, up to the top of a chosen bracket and no further. See Roth conversion room.

**Bridge phase.** The years between retiring and starting Social Security, in which your savings cover all spending. In the Withdraw screen it runs from your retirement age to your claim age.

**Capital gains (long-term).** Profit from selling an investment held more than a year. Federal long-term rates are 0%, 15% or 20%, depending on income.

**Claim age.** The age at which you start Social Security, between 62 and 70.

**Council.** The tab with your AI advisors.

**Effective tax rate.** Total tax divided by total income.

**Filing status.** Single, married filing jointly, married filing separately, head of household, or qualifying widow(er). It sets your brackets and deductions.

**FRA (full retirement age).** The age at which you receive 100% of your Social Security benefit: 66 for birth years up to 1954, rising by two months a year to 66 and 10 months for 1959, and 67 for 1960 and later. Claiming earlier reduces the benefit; waiting past FRA adds 8% per year up to age 70.

**Fan chart.** The Simulate chart showing the median and the percentile bands of portfolio value over time.

**Hallucination.** When an AI states something that is not true. The app checks dollar amounts and percentages in answers to reduce this, but cannot catch every error.

**Horizon age.** The age through which Simulate checks whether your money lasts. It starts from your life expectancy ("plan through") and is adjustable from 80 to 105.

**HSA (Health Savings Account).** A tax-advantaged account for medical costs. The app treats it as Tax-Exempt.

**IRMAA.** Income-related surcharges on Medicare premiums. Not modeled by this app.

**Marginal tax rate.** The rate on your next dollar of income.

**Median.** The middle result when all simulated outcomes are sorted. Half did better, half did worse.

**MLX.** Apple's machine-learning framework. In this app, "MLX models" are open-source language models you download from Hugging Face and run on your device with MLX.

**Model server.** A program, on your own computer or another one, that runs a language model and answers questions sent to it. Longstead can use one you choose (Ollama, LM Studio or another). See [AI_AND_MODELS.md](AI_AND_MODELS.md).

**Monte Carlo simulation.** Running many random versions of your future market returns to see how often a plan works. Simulate runs 10,000 paths.

**Nominal dollars.** Dollars not adjusted for inflation: a price in the year it is paid. Contrast with real dollars.

**NIIT (Net Investment Income Tax).** A 3.8% federal tax on investment income above certain thresholds. The app displays the thresholds but does not include the tax in its calculations.

**Ollama.** Free software that runs open-source language models on your own computer. If it is running, Longstead can find it and use its models. See [AI_AND_MODELS.md](AI_AND_MODELS.md).

**On-device.** Run on your own phone or Mac, not on a server.

**OpenAI-compatible.** A server that answers in the same chat format (the `/v1` chat API) as OpenAI's service. Ollama and LM Studio both do. In Settings, choose **Other** (any OpenAI-compatible server) to connect any such server.

**Percentile.** The 10th percentile is the level that 10% of outcomes fall below. The Simulate chart shows the 10th, 25th, 50th (median), 75th and 90th.

**Plan health.** The share of simulated paths in which your money lasts to the horizon age. Also called success rate.

**Plan through.** The age through which you want the plan to last; stored as life expectancy in your profile.

**Planning engine.** The app's own code that computes your plan numbers (the chance your savings last, median ending balance, net worth, debts, income). It runs 10,000 trials with a fixed random seed, so the same plan gives the same number. The AI does not do this math.

**Pre-RMD phase.** The years after the Bridge phase and before required minimum distributions begin.

**Provisional income.** The figure used to decide how much of your Social Security is taxable: your other income plus half of your benefits. Taxable portion is 0% below the first threshold, up to 50% between thresholds, and up to 85% above the second. Thresholds are $25,000 / $34,000 for single, head-of-household and qualifying widow(er), and $32,000 / $44,000 for married filing jointly.

**Real dollars.** Dollars adjusted to today's purchasing power. Simulate uses real dollars, so inflation is already accounted for and your spending stays constant.

**Required inputs.** The five details the planner needs before it gives a plan figure: current age, retirement age, yearly spending, filing status, and savings in at least one account. Everything else is optional and never blocks an answer.

**RMD (required minimum distribution).** The amount the IRS requires you to withdraw each year from tax-deferred accounts such as traditional IRAs and 401(k)s, starting at 73 (born before 1960) or 75 (born 1960 or later), calculated as the balance divided by an IRS life-expectancy divisor. Missing one can bring a penalty.

**RMD phase.** In the Withdraw screen, the years from the RMD start age up to age 80 (or later if RMDs start after 80).

**Roth conversion.** Moving money from a tax-deferred account to a Roth account and paying tax on the amount moved now, in exchange for tax-free growth and withdrawals later.

**Roth conversion room.** How much you can convert this year before your taxable income passes the top of a chosen bracket, with the tax that costs. See [USER_GUIDE.md](USER_GUIDE.md).

**Sequence-of-returns risk (sequence risk).** The risk that poor market returns early in retirement do more damage than the same returns later, because you are withdrawing money while balances are low.

**Standard deduction.** A fixed amount subtracted from income before tax. The app uses it (with an extra amount for ages 65 and up) and does not model itemized deductions.

**Success rate.** See Plan health.

**Tax-deferred.** Taxed when you withdraw: traditional 401(k), traditional IRA, 403(b), 457(b). Shown as Tax-Deferred.

**Tax-exempt.** In this app, an HSA: no tax on contributions, growth, or qualified medical withdrawals.

**Tax-free.** Roth accounts: contributions are taxed up front, and qualified withdrawals are not taxed. Shown as Tax-Free.

**Taxable account.** A regular brokerage or savings account. You pay tax on interest, dividends and gains as they occur.

**Tool (AI tool).** One of the app's built-in calculators that an advisor can call, such as the federal tax calculator. Tools produce the figures; the AI explains them.

**Treatment (tax treatment).** Which of the four categories an account falls into: Tax-Deferred, Tax-Free, Taxable, or Tax-Exempt.

**Trial / path.** One simulated future in a Monte Carlo run.

**Volatility.** How much returns swing year to year, measured as a standard deviation. The default is 15%.

**Withdrawal order.** The sequence of accounts you draw from. A common approach is taxable first, then tax-deferred, then Roth, but the best order depends on your situation.

_Not financial advice. Longstead gives educational estimates, not financial, tax, or legal advice. Check important figures with a qualified professional._
